subject.title: [Feature]: Capability-based permissions for skills/tools (default-deny high-risk actions)

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class core capability manifest, grant, enforcement, and audit layer for skills/tools, and what is the smallest approved first slice?
rationale: This changes public plugin/skill contracts, persisted policy or grant state, default-deny behavior, and security enforcement boundaries, so automation cannot choose the product/security model safely.

options.title: Stage Core Capability Contract
options.body: Approve a schema/parser/diagnostics first slice, then design grants, pre-model filtering, execution-boundary checks, and audit as separate reviewed phases.

options.title: Audit-Only Manifests For Now
options.body: Accept only visibility and install-policy propagation while explicitly deferring grants and enforcement to later RFCs.

options.title: Governance Plugins Only
options.body: Keep enforcement outside core and treat before_tool_call governance plugins as the supported path, leaving this core issue closed or superseded.

recommendation.title: Stage Core Capability Contract
recommendation.body: Approve a schema/parser/diagnostics first slice, then design grants, pre-model filtering, execution-boundary checks, and audit as separate reviewed phases.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest observed current-source and issue-discussion connection to plugin/tool/gateway security boundary decisions.
